Docs/Felix Agentic Analyst/Start Here/Start here 
Start here 
Updated October 30, 20265 min readCopy link
Felix is the analyst, agent and partner built into Quantum Metric. It answers questions about the experience data you already capture, runs analyses on a schedule, applies the definitions you give it, and turns what it finds into something you can share.
What Felix is
Felix works in three ways. As an analyst, it investigates what changed in your experience and proposes why. On a schedule, it works as an agent: it analyzes your pages, funnels and KPIs, can score what it finds against criteria you set, and emails you the result. It also works as a partner that keeps the definitions you give it and applies them in Chat, Copilot and Background Agents.
"Agentic" describes how it gets there. Felix decides how to approach a question and works through it with the data and tools it has. It plans the analysis, runs the queries, and shows you the analytics queries it ran, with the data they returned. You ask in plain language, and Felix works out which of your events, metrics and Business Concepts fit the question.
Felix's session summaries, user summaries and the answers in the session grid are separate, generative features. They are not part of Felix Agentic, and these pages don't cover them.
Five ways to work with Felix
What it does
Reach for it when
Use something else when
Chat
A full-page conversation over your data. Attach files, reference your dashboards, funnels, metrics, segments, cards, workflows and past queries by name, and point Felix at a Skill.
You have a question, or an investigation you want to steer.
You want the same analysis every week (Background Agents), or you're already looking at a dashboard (Copilot).
Copilot
Chat opened beside the page you're on, with that page already in the conversation. Available on dashboards and other analysis pages.
You want to know what's on screen, why a number moved, or how two variants compare.
The question isn't about the page in front of you (Chat).
Background Agents
An analysis Felix runs on a schedule, can score against criteria you set, and emails you.
You're watching a page, a funnel or a KPI, or repeating a check you'd otherwise rebuild by hand.
It's a one-off question (Chat), or you want a report your Quantum Metric team set up, with the same steps every run (Workflows).
Workflows
A defined, repeatable analysis: a Report with charts, tables and narrative, or an Automation that takes an action.
You want a report your Quantum Metric team set up, with the same steps every run, or a result should trigger an action.
The question is still exploratory, or you'll change it often (Chat).
Artifacts
What Felix made, saved and shared: a report, a chart or an export, with the steps that built it attached and a link others can open.
You're handing a result to someone, or asking a follow-up about a result you were sent.
You want Felix to keep watching (Background Agents), or you haven't run the analysis yet (Chat).
If you're not sure where to start:
For an ad-hoc question, use Chat.
For a question about the dashboard in front of you, use Copilot.
For anything recurring or unattended, use a Background Agent.
For a report your Quantum Metric team set up, with the same steps every run, use a Workflow.
For a result you want to keep or hand to someone, use an Artifact.
These build on each other. Design an analysis in Chat and share the result as an Artifact. Once the structure settles, your Quantum Metric team can turn it into a Workflow, and a Background Agent can run it on a schedule. Today they build Workflows with you; you run them, read the results and export their definitions.
What shapes Felix's answers
You can change two things that shape Felix's answers, and your Quantum Metric team sets up a third.
A Skill is a set of instructions and resources that Felix loads to answer a specific kind of question. Built-in Skills cover common kinds of analysis, such as root cause analysis, funnel analysis and error investigation, and some are written for a particular industry and apply to subscriptions in it. Your team can write its own and publish them to your workspace or subscription. On every message, Felix looks for the Skills that best match and loads one only when it decides to use it.
Directives are standing instructions Felix keeps at the private, workspace or subscription level. This is how your definition of a metric becomes Felix's definition. Add "Conversion rate is unique converted users divided by unique users" as a Directive, and your conversations from then on use it. A private Directive applies from your next conversation. A Directive you suggest for your team goes to review before it applies to anyone else. Felix is instructed to treat subscription-level Directives as overriding workspace ones, and workspace ones as overriding private ones. Directives apply in Chat, Copilot and Background Agents.
Business Concepts are the mapping of your events and terms that your Quantum Metric team configures, so Felix uses your business's terms for your data.
What Felix can see
Felix reasons over data that meets four conditions. When an answer comes back empty or a number looks wrong, check these first.
Condition
What it means
Captured
Quantum Metric records it from your site or app.
Mapped
It has a name Felix can use: an event, a metric or a Business Concept.
Retained
It falls inside your subscription's retention window.
Permitted
Your own access allows it.
If any of the four is missing, Felix can't analyze that data, however the question is phrased.
Every question runs inside the workspace you're in. Switch workspaces to change what Felix looks at.
Copilot starts from a summary of the view on screen, not the full dataset behind it, and runs a query when the summary isn't enough. If you send too many requests in a short time, Felix shows "Too many requests" and asks you to wait a moment and try again.
Felix's answers to the same question may differ between runs; when Felix runs a query, check the query and the data shown with the answer. In a Workflow, the data steps run the same queries in the same way every run; steps that write text, such as a narrative summary, may vary.
Access
Your Quantum Metric admin grants Felix per person. Three permissions decide what you see: Chat, which includes Workflows, Skills, Directives and Artifacts; Background Agents; and Copilot.
Felix appears as Felix AI in the left navigation. If you have the Background Agents permission without Chat, Felix AI opens your list of Background Agents.
Where to go next
Chat: ask questions, steer an investigation, and turn what you find into a Skill or an Artifact.
Copilot: the same conversation, started from the page you're on.
Background Agents: schedule an analysis, set the criteria, and get the result by email.
Workflows: repeatable reports and automations your Quantum Metric team builds with you.
Artifacts: save, share and revisit what Felix made, with the steps that built it.
Skills: the expertise Felix applies, built in and your own.
Directives: standing instructions that make your definitions Felix's definitions.
MCP: connect your own scripts, pipelines and other agents to Quantum Metric through the MCP Server, using an integration token.
